title: The Father at His Source and the Proprium that Counterfeits Him
summary: A parallel meditation on the Lord at his inmost set against the proprium's autogenesis from itself, with the bridging emanations between. T19 explains why the Lord at every register where he stands as foundation is named Father; T20 expounds the First Father in his five members and the five attributes proceeding from him; T21 describes the Land of Light where nothing grows except what the Lord has given; T22 contrasts what stands from before eternity with what has its end already prepared. T23 traces how Hyle, the Enthumesis of Death, molds a counterfeit cosmos from herself alone; T24 unfolds the measured times of regeneration against the unmeasurable Lord. T25 names the Lord's five emanations going forth one beside another from the five faculties of the inmost; T26 likens the First Man, the Ambassador, and the Splendor as one redemption in three registers; T27 anatomizes the body the proprium takes when it has come into its strength — five forms answering to the rational's five degrees.
organizing_principle: Parallel treatment of divine source and self-claimed source: T19-T22 expound the Father at his inmost as the standing source from which everything proceeds; T23-T24 expound the proprium claiming itself as source from itself with no fellow; T25-T27 show the bridging emanations — the Lord's five going forth (T25), three likenesses of his coming (T26), and the proprium's parody body in five forms (T27). The structural pattern is divine source vs. self-claimed source, with intermediating emanations that show the proprium imitating what it cannot receive.
